collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager still remembers a stranger once saying they had kind hands: tell a friend, or pass a kind word on.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: When (subject) was young, someone (subject.he/she) barely knew watched (subject.him/her) bandage a child's knee and said, in passing, "You've got kind hands." That was all. They probably forgot it the next minute. Today, bandaging another scraped knee, (subject) realizes (subject.he/she) has thought about that sentence almost every day of (subject.his/her) life since.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) tells (friend) about it. "Isn't it strange? A stranger said four words to me, and I've been trying to live up to them ever since." (friend) thinks about it, then says, "Well. You have kind hands." (subject) laughs. "Don't. I'll be stuck with that one too." But (subject.he/she) smiles about it all evening.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) decides to do the same thing for somebody else. At the fire that night, (subject.he/she) watches (young_villager), a young villager, patiently untangling a toddler's hair, and says, as lightly as (subject.he/she) can, "You're very patient." (young_villager) looks startled, then pleased. (subject) has no idea if it'll stick. (subject.He/she) hopes it might.
